frontier.hypothesis: Target's use-once preheader copy is emitted by jump.c or flow.c - the last two unread emit_move_insn/gen_move_insn producers in the s28 census - rather than surviving combine at all, which would explain why 31 sessions of combine-escape spellings have never reproduced it without paying a second use or a pseudo merge.
frontier.mechanism: s28's census enumerated seven copy producers in GCC 2.7.2 (loop.c 14, reload1.c 13, unroll.c 9, jump.c 7, integrate.c 2, cse.c 1, flow.c 1); loop.c, reload1.c and integrate.c are closed by measurement in s28/s29/s30 and unroll.c never runs here (no unrolling in the target stream). jump.c's move emitters run during cross-jumping / jump threading and flow.c's during life analysis, both AFTER the point where the candidate's copy would have been deleted, so either could create a copy that never faced can_combine_p. This is also the only remaining explanation consistent with s31's measured fact that target's $a3 is use-once.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/jump.c's 7 emit_move_insn/gen_move_insn call sites and flow.c's 1 end to end and identify which are reachable for this CFG (two guarded do-while loops sharing a return-0 block), exactly as s28 did for loop.c. Then run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80017848` on the candidate chassis and read tmp/grind/func_80017848/dumps/ings.jump and ings.flow for a preheader reg-reg set that is absent from ings.combine's input - the dump names the producer in one read. If both are structurally unreachable, the copy is a combine survivor after all and the only untried survival route left is the succ-based `reg_used_between_p (dest, succ, i3)` refusal at combine.c:902 (a THREE-insn combine i1/i2/i3), which no session has spelled.

frontier.hypothesis: A second use of loop 2's copy destination that cse CANNOT fold away costs less than the 6-point in-body minimum, because s31 showed the cheap sites all failed for the same removable reason (cse folded the recomputation before combine ran) rather than because the site was expensive.
frontier.mechanism: Cell P's bottom-test use (score 9) and the older in-body site (6) both re-express an expression cse already has available, so q's reference count is back to one by the time can_combine_p runs. A use cse cannot fold - one whose value is not an available expression, e.g. a comparison of q against another live pointer, or a use through a differently-typed access that cse does not treat as equivalent - would keep the reference and force the refusal without adding an instruction, provided the use itself folds into an instruction target already has.
frontier.next_probe: Price loop-2 second-use sites that are NOT redundant recomputations: (i) the loop-exit test written as a pointer comparison against a value derived from q rather than an address recompute; (ii) q used as the source of the loop's first address computation (addr = q + sh2 + i) so the use sits in an insn target already spends (addu v0,a0,v1); (iii) q consumed by loop 2's guard arm through a sub-word read of the pointer, which cse does not canonicalise to the same expression. Measure both the score AND whether `addu a3,a0,zero` appears, not just the score.

frontier.hypothesis: The three residual instructions are one decision, not two: a form whose loop-1 exit tail is a fresh `lw a0,12(s2)` necessarily loses loop 1's copy under every mechanism measured so far, so the correct move is to find the single construct that gives BOTH loops a use-once surviving copy, and to stop optimising the two loops independently.
frontier.mechanism: Target's two preheaders are byte-identical four-instruction sequences with identical seats, which is the signature of one source construct written twice; the candidate reaches 3 only by using a DIFFERENT mechanism in loop 1 (escape 1, paid for in the exit tail) than in loop 2 (nothing). Every s31 cell that made the two loops symmetric moved away from the floor (L 12, M 13, N1 30, N2 32, P 9), which is evidence that the symmetric construct is not any of the spellings tried, not that symmetry is wrong.
frontier.next_probe: Once the jump.c/flow.c producer question above is answered, re-spell the function symmetrically around whatever that answer implies and measure the two preheaders together; if the producer turns out to be a combine survivor, the symmetric construct must be one whose second use is shared - e.g. a single copy variable q defined before loop 1's guard and re-assigned in each preheader, with its downstream use in the other loop's guard - which has never been priced because it needs q live on the loop-1-skip path.
